citeAs: Clark, P., Cowhey, I., Etzioni, O., Khot, T., Sabharwal, A., Schoenick, C., and Tafjord, O. (2018). Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge. arXiv:1803.05457.
creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord (Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence)
description: The AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC) is a question set of 7,787 natural, grade-school science questions (authored for human standardized tests), partitioned into a Challenge Set (2,590 questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based and a word co-occurrence algorithm) and an Easy Set (5,197 questions). All questions are non-diagram, multiple-choice (typically 4-way), drawn from a variety of US standardized tests covering grades 3–9. The dataset is accompanied by the ARC Corpus, a 14M-sentence science text corpus, and baseline neural model implementations.
name: ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were not annotated by crowdworkers; they were sourced directly from standardized tests where correct answers were already established by the test authors/examiners. The Challenge/Easy partition was determined algorithmically: questions answered incorrectly by both the IR solver and the PMI solver were placed in the Challenge Set; the remainder formed the Easy Set.
rai:dataBiases: The Challenge Set is defined by questions that both a retrieval-based algorithm and a word co-occurrence algorithm fail to answer correctly, which means the partition only approximates the informal goal of "hard" questions and may not capture all types of difficulty. Large portions of standardized tests can be easily solved by simple AI methods, and scores on mixed datasets can be dominated by performance on easy questions, masking lack of progress on harder ones. The dataset explicitly addresses this by separating easy and hard questions. Additionally, "Mercury" questions (from an anonymous content partner) constitute the largest single source (1,762 Challenge + 3,366 Easy questions), potentially introducing source-specific biases.
rai:dataCollection: Questions were collected through several months of extensive search and investigation, drawn from a variety of US standardized tests (e.g., ACTAAP, AIMS, MCAS, NY Regents, TIMSS, and others) covering grades 3–9. The dataset includes the publicly releasable subset of the 2016 Allen AI Science Challenge (Kaggle) questions (about 60% of the Kaggle set, making up 43% of the ARC set), plus questions from an anonymous content partner ("Mercury"). All questions are non-diagram, multiple-choice natural science questions authored for human standardized tests.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions authored for US standardized science tests from a variety of sources including state assessment programs (ACTAAP, AIMS, Alaska Dept Ed, CA Standards Test, FCAT, MCAS, MEA, MEAP, MSA, NAEP, NC READY, NY Regents, Ohio Achievement Tests, TAKS, TIMSS, VA Standards of Learning, WASL) and an anonymous content partner ("Mercury") who provided science exam question data for non-commercial research purposes.
rai:dataLimitations: The Challenge Set definition (questions failed by both IR and PMI solvers) only approximates the informal goal of "hard" questions. The dataset contains only natural science questions from US grade-school standardized tests (grades 3–9), limiting domain coverage. Questions are non-diagram and multiple-choice only. The ARC Corpus, while covering ~95% of Challenge question vocabulary, may not provide sufficient signal for simple retrieval methods to answer the questions. 11 question words (mainly proper nouns) do not appear in the ARC Corpus.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were filtered to exclude diagram-based questions, retaining only non-diagram, multiple-choice questions. The dataset was partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set: the Challenge Set contains only questions answered incorrectly by both an Information Retrieval (IR) solver and a Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) solver. The question vocabulary was stemmed (6,329 distinct stemmed words).
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to drive progress in AI research toward more advanced question answering and reasoning capabilities, moving beyond factoid retrieval tasks. By using standardized test questions, it provides a measurable, motivating, and ambitious benchmark that reflects real educational assessment standards. The authors note that datasets are increasingly driving the direction of AI research, and ARC aims to redirect focus toward harder, more meaningful challenges.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended as a benchmark challenge for advanced question answering requiring knowledge and reasoning beyond simple retrieval or word co-occurrence. Designed to encourage AI research in question answering that requires reasoning, use of commonsense knowledge, and other advanced methods for deeper text comprehension. The dataset is posed as a community challenge with a public leaderboard.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: An Information Retrieval (IR) solver using Elasticsearch over the Waterloo corpus, and a Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) solver using the same corpus, were used to partition questions into Challenge and Easy sets. These two automated solvers served as filters to identify "hard" questions.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: Questions were sourced from standardized tests with pre-existing correct answers; no independent annotation per item was performed.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: No human annotators were used; questions came from standardized tests with answers established by test authors.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No crowdsourced annotation was performed; no inter-annotator agreement metrics are reported.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No annotation platform was used; questions were sourced directly from standardized tests.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not discuss missing data handling in the question collection process.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The paper only mentions "several months of extensive search and investigation" without specific dates.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation of missing values is described for this dataset.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection augmentation, balancing, or resampling of the question dataset is described.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or update cadence is described; the paper presents a fixed released dataset with a leaderboard.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of science exam questions with no personal or sensitive information about individuals.
